I'd like to preface by saying that I know this is currently a tiny community, so discussion in this thread may be slow/non-existent, but don't let that discourage you from contributing! If everyone had that thought process, nobody would ever start the conversation :)

Hi, welcome to Voat Jam! Check the sidebar for a bit more detail (not too much detail though, this sub is only 40 minutes old as I type this), but basically Voat Jam is a game jam hosted on Voat! A date's announced, then a theme, then the community makes games, plays 'em, and judges 'em!

Now, whether or not Voat Jams are 2 days long or 2 weeks long, once a month or twice a year, etc. That's up to you guys, that's what this thread's for!

The main talking points here are the following.

  • How often will Voat Jams be held?

    • This needs to be frequent enough to keep things interesting around here, but sparse enough to give everyone time to participate, and keep the event a special occasion.

  • How long will Voat Jams last?

    • Would you like something that lasts a couple days, leading to binge programming, sparked creativity, and a fast pace? Or something lasting a week or more, leading to more well thought-out games, typically of higher quality, with a slower pace?

  • How will we decide on the jam's theme?

    • I'd like this to be community picked, not sure how I want to go about it yet though. What I was considering was a thread a few days before the jam starts where you guys decide your top 5 favorite suggestions, then 1 of those is randomly selected when the jam starts. I'm definitely open to suggestions though!

Feel free to talk about other details of the jam, these are just what I thought were the most urgent off the top of my head. Be sure to subscribe if you are interested in participating in anyway, and if you have any questions, you can pm me or just reply to this post :)
Welcome to Voat Jam! Let's figure out exactly how this is going to work...

I've only done two ludum dares (and only one of them actually submitted), so I'm not fully experienced with game jams. I wouldn't mind 2 days, 4 days, or a week. Though the first time I tried I ran into real life time constraints so sometimes more time is better?

Wait a second, how will voating for game themes work? It would be cool if there was a voating system similar to what I've seen at that other place's anime place. Someone had setup a website with a voting system and had a neat gui of displaying the voting results. (It was used for things like "Best anime of the season", or something like "Best girl", you get the idea). I was imagining a voting thread where you guys just vote with upvotes. Top 5 highest suggestions are the ones that get randomly picked from. I'm definitely open to suggestions though, I know exactly what you're talking about with the anime sub, it was a cool setup, I'll have to look into it a bit more!

Have you decided on the rules of the jams? Will the jams be solo only or be able to work in teams? What libraries can be used? Just open source ones? Is Unreal Engine or Unity games allowed?

Things like that. Though I probably will go the crazy route and make games for the jam solo in C++ with SFML and my own open source "game engine" (kind of) library.

So personally I don't mind if there is a restriction on teams for the jam. The only thing I care about is being able to use my own work for making a game. I argue it's not code geared toward a specific game, but a generic game engine to be used to make any game.

I plan on posting an update tomorrow so we can get an ETA for the first jam. To answer a few of your questions, I'm thinking small teams (3 max) but that's not really an enforceable rule, so it's more of a strong suggestion, haha. And Unreal/Unity/whatever other engine you want to use is totally fine. I'll most likely be using Unity myself! :)
